findings.where: Article page specimen, the pull quote "Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!" (desktop and phone); also the motion sketch's heading "written, steady, by hand", in view beside it on desktop
findings.fault: A whole sentence of the article is set in Nanum Pen Script, at display size and on double ruled spacing. That breaks the tile's own stated rule for the hand: "one note per view, the call to action in the margin, never body text." The heading of the motion sketch is a second hand note in the same view. Read as a run of marker script, the quote is slow to read. On phone it runs to four lines with a blank ruled line between each, so the punchline falls apart.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader on an article page, who meets Mark's key line in a casual marker hand that is harder to read than the text around it and reads as a craft note, not a lawyer's argument. Angélique and the layout round would also object: the tile says the hand is kept to one margin note, while its own specimen shows it used for quotes, so they cannot tell which rule to follow.

findings.where: Every small caption block: the palette's name / hex / role captions, the stand-in print note, the texture caption, the two type-pair notes, and the motion sketch's easing line and total line (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Text of about 15 px is set on the 32 px ruled pitch, so short captions and notes look double-spaced, with each line floating alone between rules. In the motion sketch box, the table cells sit on a tighter leading that ignores the rules, while the sentences just above and below them in the same box keep the 32 px pitch. Like text in one box is set two different ways.
findings.who_objects: Anyone reading the tile, and the layout round that will build from it: the loose captions read as a list of separate fragments rather than sentences. The tile claims "the line spacing of every text block" follows the feints, yet the table breaks that claim, so the rule for setting small text is left unclear.

findings.where: Article page specimen, the headline "The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law" (desktop)
findings.fault: The article headline is set at about 36 px on two ruled lines of 64 px, so its two lines stand far apart and no longer read as one heading. The hero headline is set solid at 64/64, and the same article headline on phone is set tight. Headings of one rank get different line spacing across widths and sections.
findings.who_objects: A reader of the blog page, who sees the headline split into two separate lines with a hyphen hanging between them, and the layout round, which gets no single rule for heading leading.

findings.where: Article page specimen, the linked lecture row "Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge — Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF" (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The row's bottom border sits right on the baseline of the title's last line, so it runs through the descenders and merges with the link underline. The title looks struck through or boxed. The meta text "Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF" wraps in a narrow column and its last line hangs on that same rule.
findings.who_objects: A visitor looking for Mark's papers, who sees a cramped row whose title is cut by a line. Where the link underline ends and the border begins is unclear, so the one downloadable item on the page looks unfinished.

findings.where: Nav bar, the wordmark "MMM INFRA" beside the arches mark (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The wordmark is typed out in Libre Caslon bold capitals instead of the logo's Georgia capitals. Next to the real mark, the logo lockup becomes a redrawn wordmark in another face.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose brief says the logo stays and whose wordmark is Georgia. A visitor who knows his current site would see a slightly different logo.

findings.fault: The easing value is set in the browser's default monospace, a third, unchosen typeface inside the tile that defines a type pair.
findings.who_objects: A designer reading the tile as the type spec, who meets a face nobody chose that clashes with the Caslon around it.
